outline: This graduate-level course examines e-Business management from both managerial and research perspectives. The course covers digital transformation, digital platforms, enterprise systems, data-driven management, emerging technologies, and Generative AI applications. In addition to lectures and case studies, students will critically read and analyze international journal articles, lead paper presentations, participate in research seminars, and evaluate research methods, findings, limitations, and implications. Special attention will be given to emerging technology trends and their impacts on organizations, business models, and future research.
schedule:
Week 1. Introduction to e-Business Management and Digital Transformation

Week 2. Digital Economy, e-Business Models, and Emerging Business Trends

Week 3. Digital Platforms, Ecosystems, and Platform Strategy

Week 4. Enterprise Systems, ERP, and Digital Integration

Week 5. Digital Supply Chains and Smart Operations

Week 6. Data-Driven Management and Business Analytics

Week 7. International Journal Reading: How to Read and Analyze Academic Papers

Week 8. Research Seminar I: Journal Paper Presentation and Critical Discussion

Week 9. Emerging Technologies and Digital Business Innovation

Week 10. Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Business Applications

Week 11. Generative AI: Technologies, Applications, and Business Transformation

Week 12. Generative AI for Knowledge Work, Decision-Making, and Research

Week 13. AI Agents, Agentic AI, and Intelligent Business Automation

Week 14. Research Seminar II: Critical Analysis of Emerging Technology Research

Week 15. Research Seminar III: Student-Led Journal Paper Presentations and Discussion

Week 16. Future of e-Business: Research Trends, Opportunities, and Research Agenda

flexible_learning.content: Students will conduct an in-depth analysis of selected international journal articles related to e-Business, digital transformation, emerging technologies, or Generative AI. They will critically evaluate the research questions, theoretical foundations, methodology, findings, limitations, and contributions, and develop future research directions through seminar discussions and presentations.
flexible_learning.outcome: Students will present and critically review selected international journal articles and participate in research seminars. Learning outcomes will be assessed based on the quality of literature analysis, critical thinking, understanding of research methodology, ability to identify research gaps, discussion performance, and the development of meaningful future research questions.
flexible_learning.assessment_ratio: The flexible learning activities, including journal article analysis, seminar discussion, and research presentation, account for 20% of the final course grade.

assessment:
Class Participation and Research Discussion: 20%

International Journal Paper Presentation: 25%

Critical Review and Research Analysis: 25%

Final Research Project and Presentation: 30%

notes: This course is conducted in English and designed as a research-oriented graduate seminar. Students are expected to actively participate in discussions, critically analyze international journal articles, and present research papers in English. Generative AI tools may be used to support literature analysis and research exploration; however, students are responsible for verifying AI-generated information and demonstrating independent critical thinking.
